newsitem.title: GEORGIA: GOLF-TIGER ROARS INTO MASTERS FINAL ROUND WITH RECORD LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER ROARS INTO MASTERS FINAL ROUND WITH RECORD LEAD.

text.p: Tiger Woods, displaying the cool bravado of a bullfighter and the delicate precision of a surgeon, methodically overpowered the Augusta National golf course Saturday to lead the Masters by a record nine strokes after three rounds.

The 21-year-old Woods, playing only his third Masters, shot a flawless seven-under-par 65 to tie the Masters 54-hole scoring record and leave the world's best golfers bobbing in his wake and struggling to find superlatives to describe their young rival.

It was the second consecutive day that Woods, making his Masters debut as a professional, posted the best round of the day following his 66 on Friday, when he became the youngest player ever to lead the tournament.
"He is like a boy amongst men and showing the men how to play," 47-year-old Tom Watson said after shooting a three-under-par 69 to move into a fourth-place tie -- 11 shots behind Woods.
The young sensation's closest pursuer was Costantino Rocca of Italy, who posted a rollercoaster 70 that gave him a 210 total and the honour of playing with Woods in the final round.
Rocca, however, was not optimistic about overtaking the leader. "Catch Tiger? Maybe if I play nine holes -- under par, too," the Italian joked.
Paul Stankowski shot 69 to stand third, 10 shots off the pace, followed by veterans Tom Kite, who shot 66, and Watson.

Woods, seeking to become the youngest Master champion, jumped out to a fast start and never looked back as the other 45 players failed to mount any kind of charge on a relatively benign golf course that was softened by overnight rain.

The three-time U.S. Amateur champion made four birdies on Augusta National's usually tough front nine and then added three more coming home, including one at the last, to take the biggest lead ever into the final round of the Masters.
The previous biggest 54-hole lead was fashioned by Raymond Floyd in 1976 on his way to the tournament scoring record of 271.

"I'm really surprised that nobody made a run," Woods said after his amazing run of birdies, in which he used his awesome length off the tee to reduce Augusta's famed 6,925-yard layout into something resembling a pitch-and-putt course.
"Right now I'm capitalising on my advantage," said Woods, whose drives average well over 300 yards.
"If I drive the ball well, I can be aggressive, spin the ball (on approaches) and hold my distances."
And that was exactly what he did.

He hit irons on his second shot on all four par-5s -- making birdies on three -- and wedges to the greens on most of the par-4s. He failed to birdie the 485-yard par-5 13th when he drove into trees on the right and went over the green with his second.

Rocca, a European Ryder Cup player who lost a playoff to John Daly in the 1995 British Open, gained second place by shooting five-under-par 31 on the back nine, where he made up five strokes in four holes, including two birdies and an eagle on the 11th through 13th holes -- Augusta's famed Amen Corner.
Stankowski also eagled the 13th hole and made a spectacular par save on the 500-yard 15th, where he hit his second shot over the green and into a pond behind it.
"That was the shot of my career," he said of his pitch to within tap-in distance for par.
Woods meanwhile was piling up the first of what promises to be many Masters records that he will compile in years to come.

In addition to his record nine-stroke advantage after three rounds and his record-tying 201 total -- matching Floyd's in 1976 -- Woods also posted the lowest total for the second and third rounds of the Masters, 13-under-par 131.
Woods was not concerned about records, however.
"The only thing I want is a green jacket in my closet," he said -- before hurrying off to the practice range.
